name: Gardner Syndrome
aliases: Familial Polyposis Coli with Soft Tissue Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps
Presence of osteomas, especially of the skull and jaw
Presence of soft tissue tumors such as epidermoid cysts or fibromas
Positive family history of Gardner syndrome or familial adenomatous polyposis
Identification of pathogenic APC gene mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps and osteomas, or identification of pathogenic APC gene mutation with clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for APC mutations is highly recommended for confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Osteomas of the skull and jaw
searchTerms: benign bone tumors on skull and jaw
bony growths in head and jaw bones
dental problems like extra or stuck teeth

common.symptomName: Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
searchTerms: thickened pigment layer in retina from birth

rare.symptomName: Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium with visual impairment
searchTerms: birth-related retinal pigment changes causing vision problems
congenital retinal pigment hypertrophy with vision loss

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic APC gene mutation
Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) in colorectal cancer
imaging: CT or MRI showing multiple osteomas in skull and jaw
Colonoscopy revealing numerous colorectal adenomatous polyps
Ultrasound or MRI detecting desmoid tumors
genetic: Germline mutation in APC gene on chromosome 5q21-q22
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathology of polyps showing adenomatous changes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps without extracolonic manifestations such as osteomas or soft tissue tumors
Hamartomatous polyps rather than adenomatous polyps

redFlags: Development of colorectal cancer at young age
Rapid growth of desmoid tumors causing organ compression
Multiple osteomas causing facial deformities or functional impairment
references: NORD - National Organization for Rare Disorders: Gardner Syndrome
